doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Return to New York in the late 1960s
title: Sonny Rollins at the Vanguard and being told he plays too much
summary: Ware and Al Foster play with Rollins; Tony Williams says they will be fired for playing too much, and they are.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I know one night Tony Williams was in the house. Miles was in the house, too, you know. He was kind of in his bag. He was, you know, just standing around. He was speaking and whatnot. Sonny was staring standing off into space and Al Foster and I come out -- we had a beautiful set -- come off the stand, come back in the kitchen. Tony Turner say, "You guys are cats
going to get fired." I say, "For what, man?" He say, "You're playing too much."

And sure enough, we didn't have a gig the next week. But that was all right. Sonny had a thing. He had a thing, he told me, the last time I played with him, we went to play a benefit over in Newark. This was about '72. He say, "Wilbur, you ain't going to start on me tonight." I never looked at it that way. I figured that whenever you get up on the bandstand, you do your best and you put your best foot forward and it wasn't that I would try to outplay anybody. If I'm happy, he's inspiring me and I'm going to inspire him. Piano players, the drummer, whatever, I'm going to play my best, regardless. That's the way I feel. It's the only way I could play.
It's funny. If the band around me, if they not playing, I can't play.
